releases.summary: Rewrite the specification and design books from the current code as Markdown; keep only the current baseline in the tree (earlier versions via tags); neutral example values; retire the v1.1 contracts. Fixes: kept protection plans count in the portfolio stress limit; console next-page cursors, stale panels after a failed request and judgment-page export; oversized provider responses are delivery-unknown.
Strategy store: a failed binding query reports STORE_UNAVAILABLE instead of OBJECT_BINDING_CHANGED; only a missing or different binding is a binding change.

Application instance: when no new batch may open (risk fraction not above zero, or every hard stop beyond the insurance stop), the still-valid initial-distance directive is withdrawn by a newer one without a risk fraction, so the strategy layer opens no batch from the old one. Documentation describes local configuration, prompts and credentials in plain terms; unused test fixtures removed.

Layers become an abstract dependency order registered in doc/layers.json: trading, strategy, application and operations, each holding any number of modules and specs. The web console and model access move to the operations layer (src/factorforge/operations). The application module is renamed soxl. The unused event-analysis path and the watchlist are removed from the application, its read API and the console; the application now provides news judgment, stop and position management and scheduled calendars.
Calendar worker: a Treasury auction listed without an auction date yet no longer invalidates the whole page and stops the schedule update; it is skipped until the date is published.

The application specification drops requirements that its code never implemented (product and price handling, quota and account-protection duplicates of the trading layer, restart verification, model budget, self-granted eligibility) and the matching acceptance rows; a prompt-file acceptance test is added. Contribution rules now require a requirement change to ship with its code and tests in the same pull request.

Trading layer: a starting executor takes over an expired lease by itself when it can prove the previous holder's process is gone (host rebooted, or the process exited in the same boot), so a host reboot no longer leaves executors waiting for a manual fence. Without that proof the manual fence is still required. Takeover evidence is stored with the lease and audited.

Web console: the market chart on the dynamic page can show 24 hours, 3 days, 7 days or all history. Longer ranges read the trading layer's 5-minute final bars page by page and merge only complete buckets into coarser bars in the browser; a bucket with a missing bar is not drawn. The capabilities response now carries max_limit so the browser pages within the configured limit.

Web console: on the dynamic page, the judgment arrows and the entry/exit squares on the market chart now cover the chart's selected range instead of only the last 72 hours, and the page says so when there is no position and therefore no stop lines.

Trading layer: an executor whose lease lapsed because it was itself blocked (a slow venue call, a stalled host) renews it and keeps running, as long as nobody took the lease and the epoch was not isolated. Before, the loop renewal treated its own lapsed lease as a previous executor that was not isolated and exited. A different holder, a newer epoch or an isolated epoch still stops the executor with EXECUTOR_LEASE_LOST.

Trading layer: the protection and executor workers and the venue write fence now pass the same lease rule as the loop renewal. Before, they asserted a strictly valid lease, so when a venue call blocked the loop for more than a minute the executor's own lapsed lease was reported as EXECUTOR_LEASE_LOST and the executor exited, against S1-012. The fence now renews the lease in the run transaction before the change or venue call; a different holder, a newer epoch or an isolated epoch still stops the executor.

Strategy layer: when the trading layer raises the owner epoch because the object's own venue protection order filled, and the position and pending quantity are flat, the run is normal and the target is blocked only for that review, the object adopts the new epoch and leaves recovery, with an OWNER_EPOCH_ADOPTED audit. Before, no path adopted the new epoch, so after one venue stop the object stayed in recovery and could never add risk again. External facts and any other epoch change still need review, and the re-entry gate after a stop still applies.

SOXLUSDT instance: the position manager writes a batch's OPEN record before it saves its state. When that save was lost, every later cycle opened the same position cycle again at a new time and failed on DYNAMIC_RECORD_CONFLICT, so the batch's close stop and trailing stop were no longer managed. The manager now restores the batch from the OPEN record before reading candles.

Web console: the browser now has two pages with an instance switch at the top left. The live pipeline page draws the modules from news to the account with a live health and one sentence each, and opens a module's details and current parameters on click. The market and trades page shows the totals, the chart with stops and judgment marks, the current conviction with the share of each active judgment in the pool (hover shows the judgment and its news), the trades rebuilt from fills with volume, notional and realized or unrealized P&L and ratio, and the judgment and action records folded by default. The other views stay as read and export APIs. Built with Ant Design and React Flow; light and dark display.

Web console: the chart's open and close squares and the average-entry line come from the trading layer's fills and position, so a new position shows at once instead of after the instance records its batch. A narrow chart opens on the latest bars with the newest at the right edge instead of squeezing the whole day into a phone screen, and the instance switch no longer leaves a sticky tooltip on touch screens.

Strategy layer: a pre-event reduce whose target delivery is rejected is issued again at the same quantity in later cycles of the window until the position reaches it. Before, the schedule was marked handled when the reduce was decided, so a rejected delivery left the full position held into the event.

Strategy layer: command idempotency records stay in the state for 24 hours and then move to an append-only archive that replays still read, so a late replay returns the original result as before. The records had no retention, so the stored state, which a single read must keep under 16 MiB, grew with every command.

Strategy layer: a target the trading layer refuses only because its expected_version went stale is prepared again from a fresh snapshot and sent up to three times in the same delivery pass. Before, it waited for the next decision cycle, so a changed target could be held back by one or more cycles while the run's version kept moving.

Trading layer: when the combination check cannot be computed because a mark, rate or rule is unavailable (for example during a market-data gap), the account gate no longer adds a persistent PASSIVE_ risk lock; risk increases already fail for the same reason. A lock an earlier version added this way is removed at the next gate, and a run it alone locked returns to NORMAL when the resume conditions hold, otherwise to RECOVERY_CHECK. Before, a short data gap left the run RISK_LOCKED with no way back.

Application layer: an optional price-state entry gate. Every hour the position manager computes price-only features from the last ten days of hourly closes and asks a registered typed-judgment model whether the market is in an uptrend, a downtrend or a range; the request names no instrument and no time. While flat, a new batch opens only when that state agrees with the direction, otherwise the initial stop directive is withdrawn until it does; open batches are not affected. When no fresh state is available the gate either blocks new batches or lets them open as without the gate, as registered. The read API and the console show the latest state and the gate decision; hourly states are recorded but not listed as actions. Unregistered instances behave as before.

All layers: initializing a shared schema no longer locks tables that running instances write to. Triggers, indexes, row security, policies and added columns are created only when missing instead of dropped and recreated, so a deploy or a new instance re-running initialization neither waits for nor deadlocks with the instances already writing.

Trading system: a run degraded because a close filled in parts returns to NORMAL once the position is flat, the venue conditional cleanup is confirmed and every protection for the instrument is closed. Before, a flat run stayed DEGRADED and refused every new order; the executor now also restores such a run on its next idle pass.

Storage: a connection pool without pool_max_conns in its DSN holds at most 3 connections, so all service processes on one host stay under the server's max_connections; before, pgx allowed one per CPU per process and a slow disk could exhaust every connection. Trading system: the market collector also reads candles from the newest one P1 accepted from it (at most CandleRetention back, the whole retention on its first round), so an outage longer than the lookback no longer leaves a permanent candle gap that marks prices MISSING.

Strategy framework: a decision's stored input keeps the trading snapshot's fills and funding incomes as a count and digest, like the bars and source decisions. Both lists are the run's whole history, so each retained decision grew with every trade and settlement; the input hash is still taken over the complete inputs and P1 keeps the rows.

Strategy framework: listing an object's stop directives takes scope=current, which returns the head directives and the last effective strategy stop in one page. SOXLUSDT instance: the position manager reads its effective stop that way instead of paging through the whole list, which keeps every superseded directive; after a month of initial-distance refreshes it exceeded the page budget, the effective stop went missing, and close-stop exits, baseline transfer and settled trailing stops stopped working.
